hunks.baseline: Human beings possess possibilities close to infinite.
hunks.sol: Human beings possess almost limitless potential.

hunks.baseline: With their capacity for thought surpassing that of any other living thing on Earth, they built systems of their own and developed civilization.
hunks.sol: With minds more capable than those of any other living thing on Earth, they built systems of their own and developed civilization.

hunks.baseline: From the utterly primitive prehistoric age to the present.
In particular, the history and culture humans had built over the past several thousand years were truly dazzling.
hunks.sol: From the primitive prehistoric age to the present, what humans had achieved was dazzling—especially the history and culture they had built over the past several thousand years.

hunks.baseline: Humans kept discovering new things, and moved forward with every one of them.
hunks.sol: Humans never stopped discovering new things. With each discovery, they moved forward.

hunks.baseline: Until they filled battlefields where spears and swords once clashed with the sound of gunfire, and car horns rang through streets ablaze with neon signs instead of the whinnying of horses.
hunks.sol: Until gunfire filled battlefields where swords and spears had once clashed. Until car horns replaced the whinny of horses on streets lit by neon signs.

hunks.baseline: Until they crossed five seas and six continents, and finally ventured into space.
hunks.sol: Until they crossed five seas and six continents and finally ventured into space.

hunks.baseline: On the day that grand plan, named after an ancient sun god, succeeded.

hunks.baseline: What had the god, watching from somewhere, thought at that historic moment when a human first set foot on the moon and called it “one small step, one giant leap for mankind”?
hunks.sol: On the day that grand plan, named after an ancient sun god, succeeded, what did the god watching from somewhere think? A human had set foot on the moon for the first time and called that historic moment “one small step, one giant leap for mankind.”

hunks.baseline: No one could know the will of God, but an old man with the rather long name of Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Ali could be certain.
hunks.sol: No one could know the will of God. But an old man with the rather long name Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Ali was certain.

hunks.baseline: Otherwise, He wouldn’t have unleashed a great flood called the Great Cataclysm.
hunks.sol: Otherwise, He would not have unleashed a great flood called the Great Cataclysm.

hunks.baseline: Sending the great Prophet down to this land and commanding him to punish them surely meant that he was to punish humanity’s arrogance on God’s behalf.
hunks.sol: Surely, sending the great Prophet to this land to punish them meant that the Prophet was to judge humanity’s arrogance on His behalf.

hunks.baseline: “Do you not think so as well, you sinful infidel?”
hunks.sol: “Do you not think so too, sinful infidel?”

hunks.baseline: At the old man’s calm voice, the middle-aged man trembled.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man trembled at the old man’s calm voice.

hunks.baseline: Drenched in crimson blood, he stood amid his many subordinates, who had been alive and breathing only moments ago and now lay strewn across the ground.
hunks.sol: Drenched in blood, he stood amid his many subordinates. Only moments ago, they had been alive and breathing. Now they lay strewn across the ground.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man had nothing left.
Nothing but the sword in his hand and the mana still boiling through his body, his fighting spirit undiminished.
hunks.sol: He had nothing left but the sword in his hand and the mana boiling through his body, his fighting spirit still undiminished.

hunks.baseline: “Repent through death. Like those who went before you.”
hunks.sol: “Atone through death. Like those who went before you.”

hunks.baseline: With a scream, the middle-aged man drew on every ounce of his strength and charged at the old fanatic.
hunks.sol: With a shout like a scream, the middle-aged man drew on every ounce of his strength and charged the old fanatic.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps the last strike of his life.
hunks.sol: A strike that would likely be his last.

hunks.baseline: The sword flew faster than ever before, filled with blinding aura, and—
hunks.sol: His sword flew faster than ever before, its blade blazing with aura.

hunks.baseline: A flash came out of nowhere, cleaving both the aura-wreathed sword and its wielder in two.
hunks.sol: A sudden flash cleaved through the aura-wreathed sword and its wielder alike.

hunks.baseline: As the headless corpse crumpled to the ground, something glinting fell at the old man’s feet.
hunks.sol: As the headless corpse crumpled, something glinting fell at the old man’s feet.

hunks.baseline: The old man stared at the crucifix necklace half-buried in the hot sand, then suddenly spoke.
hunks.sol: The old man stared at the crucifix necklace half-buried in the hot sand, then spoke.

hunks.baseline: The young man who had cut down the middle-aged A-rank Hunter as casually as breathing continued,
hunks.sol: The young man who had cut down the middle-aged A-rank Hunter as easily as breathing continued, “Amir, there are more infidels not far from here. If you let me go…”

hunks.baseline: “Amir, there are more infidels not far from here. If you let me go…”

hunks.baseline: “Their main force will have heard from them on the radio this time. We’ve dealt with them easily so far, but that ends now.”
hunks.sol: “Their main force will have heard from them over the radio this time. We’ve dealt with them easily so far, but it won’t be that simple from now on.”

hunks.baseline: “Hamid, son of Hassan, you’re right. But have you forgotten what the Prophet said?”
hunks.sol: “You’re right, Hamid, son of Hassan. But have you forgotten what the Prophet said?”

hunks.baseline: At the old man’s piercing gaze, the young man named Hamid flinched without meaning to. Then, realizing the meaning of his words a moment later, his eyes widened.
hunks.sol: Hamid flinched at the old man’s piercing gaze. A moment later, he realized what Amir meant, and his eyes widened.

hunks.baseline: “If you mean what the Prophet said, then could it be…?”
hunks.sol: “What the Prophet said… Could it be?”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. The time has finally come. The time promised by the Prophet, by almighty Allah, has arrived.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. The time has finally come. The time promised by the Prophet and almighty Allah is upon us.”

hunks.baseline: Amazement turned to joy. Joy to fervor.
hunks.sol: Surprise turned to joy. Joy to fervor.

hunks.baseline: Watching the young man’s expression change by the second, the old man smiled. Then he looked down at the warriors of God surrounding them and muttered,
hunks.sol: The old man smiled as he watched Hamid’s expression change. Then he looked over the warriors of God surrounding them and murmured, “Inshallah. The Prophet will lead us to the promised land!”

hunks.baseline: “Inshallah. The Prophet will lead us to the promised land!”

hunks.baseline: With their enormous voices rising as one, the many fanatics who had lain dormant deep in the desert for decades began their advance.
hunks.sol: Their voices rose together in a mighty shout. The countless fanatics who had lain dormant deep in the desert for decades began their advance.

hunks.baseline: Toward that place overflowing with God’s grace.
hunks.sol: Toward the place overflowing with God’s grace.

hunks.baseline: If this world were a chessboard, what would my role be?
hunks.sol: If this world were a chessboard, what piece would I be?

hunks.baseline: A pawn that can only move forward?
hunks.sol: A pawn that could only move forward?

hunks.baseline: A knight that can leap farther than a pawn?
hunks.sol: A knight that could go farther than a pawn?

hunks.baseline: A bishop that traverses the board diagonally?
hunks.sol: A bishop crossing the board diagonally?

hunks.baseline: Maybe a rook that moves in straight lines, a queen with the combined power of a bishop and a rook, or, ironically, the king—both the most important piece and weaker than the queen.
hunks.sol: Maybe a rook moving in straight lines, a queen with the combined reach of a bishop and a rook, or the king—ironically, the most important piece and yet weaker than the queen.

hunks.baseline: Even now, as the Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation, even with everyone in the world knowing who I was, I still didn’t know exactly where I stood.
hunks.sol: Even now that I was Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation, even with everyone in the world knowing my name, I still didn’t know exactly where I stood. Or what I could and couldn’t do on this chessboard.

hunks.baseline: Or how far I could go on this chessboard.

hunks.baseline: But there was one thing I could say for sure.
hunks.sol: But one thing I could say for sure.

hunks.baseline: If that chessboard wasn’t called the world, but the battlefield, then I could dominate it.
hunks.sol: If that chessboard was a battlefield rather than the world, I could dominate it.

hunks.baseline: I could keep pushing forward like a pawn, then become a knight and leap over the enemy’s heads; I could range across the board in every direction like a bishop, rook, or queen, and swallow everything whole.
hunks.sol: I could push forward like a pawn, leap over my enemies’ heads like a knight, then range across the board like a bishop, rook, or queen and swallow everything in my path.

hunks.baseline: Flesh and bone burst apart before the spearhead even touched them. A Troll’s body, its upper half blown away, fell like a rotten log, and someone shouted behind me.
hunks.sol: Flesh and bone burst apart before the spearhead even touched them. A Troll with its upper half blown away toppled like a rotten log, and someone shouted behind me.

hunks.baseline: “Damn it! How many times do I have to tell you that if you kill them like that, they’re no use as undead!”
hunks.sol: “Damn it! How many times do I have to tell you? Kill them like that and I can barely use them as undead!”

hunks.baseline: Instead of answering, I twisted my body.
hunks.sol: Instead of answering, I twisted aside.

hunks.baseline: The ogres blinked stupidly, realizing what had happened a beat too late.
hunks.sol: The ogres blinked stupidly, a beat too late to understand what had happened.

hunks.baseline: But White Flame’s spearhead had already swept past their necks.
hunks.sol: White Flame’s spearhead had already swept past their necks.

hunks.baseline: Three heads flew into the air, severed from their massive bodies.
hunks.sol: Three heads flew free of their massive bodies.

hunks.baseline: I sprang off the corpse of an ogre whose life had already left it, then plunged down toward the monsters packed tightly around me.
hunks.sol: I sprang off an ogre’s lifeless corpse and plunged toward the monsters packed around me.

hunks.baseline: Blood sprayed and flesh split.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed. Flesh split.

hunks.baseline: Ding. Ding, ding.
hunks.sol: *Ding. Ding, ding.*

hunks.baseline: As System alerts reached my ears without pause, I plunged through the thick cloud of dust.
hunks.sol: System alerts rang in my ears without pause as I leaped into the thick cloud of dust.

hunks.baseline: Stowed away, then summoned in the same instant.
hunks.sol: One weapon stored, another summoned at the same instant.

hunks.baseline: White Flame vanished from my hand like an illusion, replaced by two short daggers that firmly filled my empty palms.
hunks.sol: White Flame vanished from my hand like an illusion. In its place, two short daggers settled firmly into my hands.

hunks.baseline: Among those who had used weapons like these, there was someone I’d watched up close who had earned the epithet Slaughter Saint with a single dagger.
hunks.sol: I’d watched someone wield a dagger like this up close. With a single blade, he had earned the name Slaughter Saint.

hunks.baseline: *I watched him from right beside him.*
hunks.sol: *And I watched him do it from right beside him.*

hunks.baseline: I calmed my internal energy, pounding as if it would burst, and kept my toes light and my shoulders loose.
hunks.sol: I calmed the internal energy pounding as though it would burst out of me. Light on my toes. Shoulders loose.

hunks.baseline: Remembering the Slaughter Saint’s advice, I imitated the movements I’d seen him perform right in front of me dozens of times.
hunks.sol: Remembering the Slaughter Saint’s advice, I copied the movements I’d seen him perform right in front of me dozens of times.

hunks.baseline: The wind, which had always slammed into me with force, scattered softly.
hunks.sol: The wind that had always struck me head-on now slipped gently past.

hunks.baseline: It felt as if I were floating through the air in zero gravity.
hunks.sol: I felt as though I were floating through the air in zero gravity.

hunks.baseline: Of course, I couldn’t claim I’d perfectly copied the Slaughter Saint’s personal martial art just by doing this much. But for dealing with these bastards right now, this much was enough.
hunks.sol: Of course, I couldn’t claim I’d mastered the Slaughter Saint’s personal martial art from this much. But this much was enough to deal with the bastards in front of me.

hunks.baseline: Only after flesh and bone had been cut through did the sound of slicing reach my ears.
hunks.sol: The sound of slicing reached my ears only after flesh and bone had been cut.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t that the sound was slow.
hunks.sol: Sound wasn’t slow.

hunks.baseline: I was simply that fast—the daggers in my hands were moving fast enough to leave the sound behind.
hunks.sol: I was fast enough to leave it behind. So were the daggers in my hands.

hunks.baseline: Seeping in like mist, then stabbing and slashing like flashes of light, the two daggers sent dozens of monsters crashing down in sprays of blood.
hunks.sol: I slipped among the monsters like mist, my daggers stabbing and slashing in flashes. Dozens fell, spraying blood.

hunks.baseline: No—in truth, they fell and rose again at the very same moment.
hunks.sol: No—they fell and rose again at the same moment.

hunks.baseline: A voice that seemed to reverberate inside my head rather than my ears rang out, and a chilling cold swept across the battlefield.
hunks.sol: A voice seemed to ring inside my head rather than reach my ears, and a chilling cold swept across the battlefield.

hunks.baseline: It raised the monsters that had fallen moments ago and the ones falling even now.
hunks.sol: It raised the monsters that had fallen moments ago and those falling even now.

hunks.baseline: An eerie light glimmered deep within their eyes.
hunks.sol: An eerie light glimmered deep in their eyes.

hunks.baseline: The undead army, reborn as new beings at the edge of death, charged without a moment’s hesitation at the monsters surging in from every direction, obeying their king’s command.
hunks.sol: Reborn as new beings at the edge of death, the undead army obeyed their king’s command. Without hesitation, they charged the monsters pouring in from every direction.

hunks.baseline: The roars of monsters that were alike yet different tangled together, and weapons swung with force slammed into one another’s bodies.
hunks.sol: The cries of living and undead monsters tangled together. Weapons swung hard into bodies on both sides.

hunks.baseline: But unlike the monsters still alive and therefore capable of feeling pain, the undead were creatures that had forgotten pain along with death.
hunks.sol: But the living monsters felt pain. The undead had forgotten it when they died.

hunks.baseline: Even with their limbs cut off by weapons flying in from all directions, even with their chests pierced through, they kept moving to the very end.
hunks.sol: Even when weapons took their limbs or pierced their chests, they kept moving to the very end.

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King had given them only one goal.

hunks.baseline: Before the magical power he had bestowed upon them ran out, before they met their second death, they had to create another soldier.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King had given them only one goal: before the magical power he had bestowed on them ran out, before they died a second death, they were to create another soldier.

hunks.baseline: A monster with its throat torn out screamed.
hunks.sol: A monster screamed as its throat was torn out.

hunks.baseline: The undead body, already missing an arm and a leg, was ripped to shreds by the enraged monsters, but that didn’t matter.
hunks.sol: The undead that had done it, already missing an arm and a leg, was ripped to shreds by enraged monsters. That didn’t matter either.

hunks.baseline: Thanks to that, I—
hunks.sol: It had bought me—

hunks.baseline: No, we—had bought a little more time.
hunks.sol: No, *us*—a little more time.

hunks.baseline: Countless bolts of lightning and flames streaked through the air.
hunks.sol: Countless bolts of lightning and tongues of flame streaked through the air.

hunks.baseline: Behind the enormous transport vehicle blocking the way like a barricade, the monsters packed in so tightly there wasn’t a gap—like the first day of an E-Mart Black Friday sale—had no choice but to take the sudden barrage of attacks head-on.
hunks.sol: Beyond the enormous transport vehicles blocking their path like barricades, the monsters were packed as tightly as shoppers at E-Mart on the first day of Black Friday. They took the sudden barrage head-on.

hunks.baseline: Screams filled the air in every direction.
hunks.sol: Screams filled the air.

hunks.baseline: Lightning seared scales and flesh, while flames seeped through the gaps and burned bones and organs.
hunks.sol: Lightning seared scales and flesh. Flames slipped through the gaps and burned bone and organs.

hunks.baseline: Many of the hundreds of monsters thrashing in agony unlike anything they had ever felt even swung their weapons at their own allies.
hunks.sol: Many of the hundreds of monsters writhing in pain unlike anything they had ever felt even swung their weapons at their own allies.

hunks.baseline: Monsters driven into each other by the ferocity of pure instinct.
hunks.sol: Seized by their own savage instincts, the monsters charged one another.

hunks.baseline: But I didn’t let my guard down for even a moment.
hunks.sol: But I didn’t let my guard down for a second.

hunks.baseline: “Hold formation! Don’t take a single step from where you are!”
hunks.sol: “Hold formation! Don’t move a single step!”

hunks.baseline: At my command, carried by internal energy, the Hunters who had been advancing in the heat of battle, caught up in the excitement of gaining the upper hand, stopped in their tracks.
hunks.sol: I drove internal energy into the command. The Hunters who had begun advancing, swept up in the heat of battle and the thrill of gaining the upper hand, stopped in their tracks.

hunks.baseline: Battle was momentum. It was flow.
hunks.sol: Battle was flow. Battle was momentum.

hunks.baseline: Against that enormous force of more than ten thousand, killing just a thousand monsters wouldn’t win this battle in an instant.
hunks.sol: Against a force of well over ten thousand, taking out a mere thousand monsters wouldn’t win us the battle all at once.

hunks.baseline: We had to win while minimizing our losses.
hunks.sol: We had to win while keeping our losses to a minimum.

hunks.baseline: The bastard who still hadn’t shown himself.
hunks.sol: The bastard who had yet to show himself.

hunks.baseline: And the S-rank monsters waiting for their moment amid that sea of monsters—or somewhere in the sky above.
hunks.sol: And the S-rank monsters waiting for their moment among that sea of beasts—or somewhere in the sky above.

hunks.baseline: And at that moment, just as I muttered those words deep in my heart—
hunks.sol: At that very moment, as the thought passed through my mind—

hunks.baseline: An immense magical power surged from far away, making the desert tremble.
hunks.sol: Immense magical power reached us from far away and began to shake the desert.
